info.title: Documents Service API
info.description: A QuivaWorks service that manages document templates, documents, and e-signature workflows. All routes are served under the `/file-generator` gateway prefix.

expressions.description: All template content uses angular expression syntax

control_structures.note: Both closing syntaxes valid; {/} is preferred

critical_rules: Missing payload fields render empty, not error
Filter parameters are positional and all required
Validate syntax at POST /templates/validate before deploying
common_mistakes: Copying GET response structure into UPDATE payloads

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: Template lifecycle — create, read, publish, validate, trigger, and delete document templates. Templates follow a **draft → published** model: writes (`POST`, `PATCH`) always target the draft version, and `POST /templates/{key}/publish` promotes the draft. Document generation only ever uses the published version, so drafts can be edited safely without affecting production output. A template's `source` is a DOCX file containing angular-expression tags rendered at trigger time.

tags.name: Documents
tags.description: Document lifecycle — read, update, and delete generated documents. A document record is created immediately when a template is triggered and is updated asynchronously: first with the generated `output.key` (an `obj://` or `kv://` storage URI) or `errors`, then with `signatures` progress as signatories sign.

tags.name: Signatures
tags.description: E-signature workflows powered by HelloSign (Dropbox Sign). Signature requests are created automatically when a triggered template defines `signatories`. Each signatory tracks a status lifecycle of `DRAFT → SENT → SIGNED`, with `EXPIRED` (validity window elapsed) and `FAILED` (delivery/signing error) as terminal failure states. Embedded signing URLs can be generated for signatures created in embedded mode.

get.description:
Retrieve a single document template by key.

Pass `?draft=true` to fetch the draft version; omit it (or set `false`) to fetch the published version. A template may exist as draft only (never published), published only (draft deleted after publish), or both — the two versions are independent records.

The returned `source.key` points at the DOCX file in `microstrate-documents` object storage bucket, that's being rendered when the template is triggered. Fields such as `output.name` and `signatories[].name`/`email` may contain expression placeholders (e.g. `{client_name}`) that are resolved against the trigger payload.

200.description: Template retrieved successfully. The example below shows a fully configured invoice template: a DOCX source rendered to PDF, a templated output filename, and one signatory whose details are resolved from the trigger payload.

patch.description:
Update an existing **draft** template. Unlike `POST /templates`, this does not check for pre-existence — it will create or overwrite the draft.

This is a merge-style upsert: the supplied fields are written over the draft's event stream, so partial bodies are fine (the example below updates only `output`). To *remove* a field entirely, use `PATCH /templates/{key}/unset` instead.

Changes are not visible to document generation until the draft is re-published via `POST /templates/{key}/publish`.

200.description: Template draft updated successfully. The response returns the messaging subject of the draft record.

delete.description:
Delete a draft or published template. Set `?draft=true` to target the draft version; omit it to target the published version. Deleting one version does not affect the other.

Deletion is implemented as a **poison-pill message** (`type: poison-pilled`) appended to the template's event stream — the underlying events are retained, but the aggregate resolves to deleted and the key disappears from list/get results. Deleting a published template immediately stops it from being triggerable.

get.description:
List all templates. Pass `?draft=true` to list draft templates instead of published ones.

The response is paged stream-style: `results_total` is the number of items in this response, `total_messages` is the total available, and `next_sequence` is the cursor for the next page.

post.description:
Create a new **draft** template. Returns `402` if a template with the same key already exists (use `PATCH /templates/{key}` to update an existing draft).

The `source` object references a DOCX file already uploaded to `microstrate-documents` object storage bucket. That file is processed by replacing tags with data from payload when the template is triggered: tags inside the DOCX (e.g. `{client_name}`, `{#line_items}…{/line_items}`, `{subtotal + tax}`) are evaluated against the trigger payload to produce the final output — a PDF when `output.content_type` is `application/pdf`, or a rendered DOCX. 

Other expression-aware fields:
- `output.name` — output filename template, e.g. `invoice-{invoice_number}`; the extension (`.pdf`/`.docx`) is appended automatically based on `output.content_type`.
- `signatories[].name` / `signatories[].email` — resolved against the payload before the Signature request is sent. Signatories whose rendered email is missing or invalid are skipped.
- `sub_templates[].conditions` — rule-engine conditions evaluated against the payload; matching sub-templates are rendered and merged after the main template.

It is recommended to run `POST /templates/validate` on the DOCX content first to catch malformed tags.

402.description: Template with this key already exists.

post.description:
Promote a draft template to published state. The published version is what `POST /templates/trigger` uses to generate documents — draft edits have no effect on generation until published.

Publishing copies the current draft aggregate to the published record; subsequent draft edits do not leak into the published version. Returns `400` if no draft exists for the key.

Validate a base64-encoded template file before storing it.

The file is checked by rendering tags with empty data, and any tag errors are returned without persisting anything. The `errors` entries are error explanations, covering problems such as unclosed loop tags, duplicate/unopened close tags, and expressions that fail to compile.

Validation is **syntactic**: it confirms the tags compile, not that the payload you eventually send will contain every referenced identifier — unresolved identifiers at trigger time render as an empty string rather than failing.

Always run this before `POST /templates` / `PATCH /templates/{key}` when the source DOCX changes — a template that stores an invalid source will fail every trigger.

invalid.description: Each entry is an error explanation for one failing tag.

errors: The tag beginning with "{#line_items" is unclosed
The scope parser for the tag "subtotal +" failed to compile

post.description:
Remove specific fields from a **draft** template by dot-notation path.

NOTE: although this is a field-removal operation, the gateway routes it as **POST** `/file-generator/templates/{key}/unset` (the document equivalent is PATCH). Each path is unset as its own `type: unset` event on the template stream. Re-publish for the change to affect generation.

Generate one or more documents from **published** templates.

Each entry in `list` names a template key and may override its stored `output` configuration. The shared `payload` object is the data context for **angular expression evaluation**: every key in the payload becomes an identifier available to tags inside the template's source DOCX, to the `output.name` filename template, to `signatories[].name`/`email`, and (as `<key>.value` facts) to `sub_templates[].conditions`. Expressions support nested property access (`{client.address.city}`), operators (`{subtotal + tax}`, `{is_overdue ? "OVERDUE" : ""}`), condition blocks (`{#discount > 0}…{/}`), loops (`{#line_items}{description} — {qty * unit_price}{/line_items}`), and the built-in filters.

**This is an asynchronous operation.** The `200` response confirms each job was queued (or reports per-template validation errors) and returns the document `subject`. A document record is created immediately with `output: null`; the trigger consumer then fetches the published template and its matching sub-templates, renders them against the payload, merges the results, and updates the record with `output.key` (the storage URI of the generated file) — or with `errors` if rendering failed. Poll `GET /documents/{key}` to observe completion. If the template defines signatories, the signature request is dispatched automatically after rendering succeeds (each signatory starts as `DRAFT`, moving to `SENT` once the request is created).

The generated file is written to `{store}://{bucket}/{filepath}` where trigger-level `output` overrides take precedence over the template's stored `output`. Buckets may target the object store (`obj://`, default) or the key-value store (`kv://`).

200.description: Trigger jobs queued. The response is per-template: entries with a `subject` were queued successfully (the subject identifies the document record to poll); entries with `errors` failed validation and no job was queued for them. A `200` therefore does not guarantee every template was triggered — check each result.

get.description:
Retrieve a single document by key.

Documents created by `POST /templates/trigger` progress through states observable here:
- **Queued**: `output: null`, `errors: null` — rendering in progress.
- **Generated**: `output.key` set to the storage URI (`obj://bucket/path` or `kv://bucket/path`) of the rendered file.
- **Failed**: `errors` populated with rendering errors; `output` stays null.
- **Signing**: `signatures` array populated once a HelloSign request is sent; each signatory's `status` advances `SENT → SIGNED` (or `EXPIRED`/`FAILED`) as webhook events arrive.

patch.description:
Create or update a document record directly. Used to manually set document metadata outside of the template trigger workflow — for example registering an externally produced file, or correcting metadata on an existing record.

The `key` is required and derives the document's storage subject. This is an upsert: it creates the record if absent and merges supplied fields if present.

delete.description:
Delete a document record. Implemented as a **poison-pill message** (`type: poison-pilled`) on the document's event stream — the record disappears from get/list results.

Note: this deletes the document *record* (metadata, signature state). The generated file referenced by `output.key` remains in object/KV storage and must be removed separately if required.

get.description:
List documents matching a subject query.

Document subjects live under `ms.document.document.>` and mirror the sanitised output filepath, with folders as subject tokens (a document written to `contracts/acme-nda-2024.pdf` lives under `contracts.acme-nda-2024.pdf` within that namespace). The required `query` parameter is appended to the namespace and supports stream wildcard patterns:
- `contracts.*` — direct children of `contracts` (single level)
- `contracts.>` — everything under `contracts` at any depth
- `invoices.2026.*` — documents in the `invoices/2026` folder

Missing `query` returns `400` with `` `query` query param is required ``.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Stream subject query filter, e.g. `contracts.*` or `contracts.>`.

patch.description: Remove specific fields from a document record by dot-notation path. Each path is unset as its own `type: unset` event. A common use is clearing `errors` and `output` before re-triggering generation for the same document key.

get.description:
Generate an embedded signing URL for a specific signature on a document, suitable for loading in an iframe.

Only available for signatures created in **embedded signing mode** (`request.is_embedded: true` on the document's signatory record). Embedded mode is an account-level configuration — all signatures of a request share it. Requesting a URL for an unknown `signature_id` or a non-embedded signature returns a `500` with the error message (e.g. `Signature url is only available in embedded mode: …`).

Embedded URLs are short-lived; generate one immediately before presenting the signing UI rather than storing it.

200.description: Embedded signing URL generated successfully. Load this URL with the HelloSign embedded JS client; it expires shortly after creation.

post.description:
Webhook endpoint for HelloSign signature events. **Called by the HelloSign platform, not by internal services** — configure it as the callback URL in the HelloSign app settings. The event arrives as a multipart form field named `json`.

Handled event types:
- `signature_request_signed` — one signatory signed; their status on the document becomes `SIGNED` (matched by signer name + email).
- `signature_request_all_signed` — all signatories signed; the fully executed PDF is downloaded from HelloSign and written back over the document's output location in storage.
- `signature_request_invalid` — the request failed; affected signatories are marked `FAILED` with the `error` field populated.

Unrecognised event types are silently ignored. Each event's `event_hash` is verified as HMAC-SHA256(`event_time` + `event_type`) using the account's HelloSign API key; events with a hash mismatch are discarded. The endpoint **always** responds `200 Hello API Event Received` regardless of processing outcome.

json.description: JSON-encoded HelloSign event payload. Contains `event` (type, time, HMAC hash) and `signature_request` (signatures with status, plus `metadata.subject` / `metadata.key` that route the event back to the originating document).

200.description: Event received. The body is the plain string `Hello API Event Received`. The handler responds `200` even when event processing fails (hash mismatch, unknown account, lookup errors) so that HelloSign does not retry — processing errors are logged server-side only.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: Account id the webhook event is routed to.

bearerAuth.description: JWT bearer token. The service engine reads only `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` and derives the account/tenant from it.

apiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key
apiKeyAuth.description: Static API key. Accepted at the gateway, which swaps it for a JWT before the service sees the request (confirmed working for reads).

DocumentKey.name: key
DocumentKey.description: Unique document key, typically a file path.

QueryDraft.name: draft
QueryDraft.description: When `true`, targets the draft version of a template. Defaults to published.

TemplateSignatoryValidity.description: How long the signatory has to complete signing, measured from when the signature request is sent. The day/week/month/year components are summed; once elapsed, the signature is marked `EXPIRED` and the HelloSign request is cancelled.

name.description: Signatory name. Supports single-brace angular expression placeholders resolved against the trigger payload, e.g. `{client_name}`. The rendered value is trimmed and truncated to 100 characters (HelloSign limit).

email.description: Signatory email. Supports single-brace angular expression placeholders resolved against the trigger payload, e.g. `{client_email}`. The rendered value is trimmed and lowercased; signatories with a missing or invalid rendered email (or empty name) are skipped — if none remain, no signature request is sent and the document's `signatures` is `null`.

order.description: Signing order index (0-based). Defaults to the signatory's position in the array.

key.description: Key of the sub-template to merge.

conditions.description: Rule-engine condition object evaluated against the trigger payload; the sub-template is only included when it resolves to true. Payload keys are exposed as facts named `<key>.value` (e.g. payload `client_region` → fact `client_region.value`).

name.description: Output filename template, rendered against the trigger payload with single-brace angular expressions (e.g. `invoice-{invoice_number}` → `invoice-INV-2026-014`). Defaults to the template key when omitted or when rendering fails. The `.pdf`/`.docx` extension is appended automatically from `content_type` — do not include it.

content_type.description: Output MIME type. DOCX sources can render to PDF or DOCX; PDF sources can only output PDF (PDF→DOCX conversion is not supported).

bucket.description: Storage bucket. May be prefixed with `obj://` (object store, default) or `kv://` (key-value store) to select the storage backend. Defaults to the service's document bucket.

folder.description: Output folder path within the bucket.

TemplateOutput.description: Where and how the rendered document is written. The final storage key is `{bucket}/{folder}/{name}.{ext}` with the extension derived from `content_type`.

source.description: Reference to the source template file in object storage (the document object store bucket). DOCX sources are processed with the angular expression parser: tags such as `{client_name}`, `{#items}…{/items}` (loops), `{price + tax}` (operators), and `{amount | formatcurrency:'EUR'}` (filters) are evaluated against the trigger payload to produce the final output. PDF sources (`application/pdf`) are passed through — and merged with sub-templates — without expression rendering, and can only output PDF.

key.description: Template file reference. Either a simple path (uses default `microstrate-documents` bucket) or a full storage URL. Formats: `templates/invoice.docx` (default) | `obj://bucket-name/path/file.docx` (object store) | `kv://bucket-name/path/file.docx` (key-value store).

content_type.description: MIME type of the source file.

signatories.description: Signatories to request e-signatures from once the document is generated. `name` and `email` support expression placeholders resolved against the trigger payload; entries whose rendered email is missing or invalid are skipped. An empty/absent array means no signature request is sent.

sub_templates.description: Additional published templates rendered with the same payload and merged after the main template in array order. Entries with `conditions` are included only when the rule-engine conditions evaluate to true against the trigger payload.

Template.description: A document template. The `source` DOCX is rendered with angular expression parser when the template is triggered; `output` controls where and in what format the rendered file is written.

TemplateUpsertRequest.description: Request body for creating or updating a template.

DocumentSignatoryRequest.description: Signature request object attached to the signatory after a HelloSign request is sent.

is_embedded.description: Whether the signing is done via an embedded iframe.

expiry.description: ISO 8601 datetime after which the signing request expires.

signed_at.description: ISO 8601 datetime when the signatory signed. Null if not yet signed.

error.description: Error message if the signature request failed.

DocumentSignatory.description: Per-signatory e-signature state on a document. Status lifecycle: `DRAFT` (created at trigger time, request not yet sent) → `SENT` (HelloSign request dispatched; `request` populated) → `SIGNED`, or `EXPIRED` (validity window elapsed — an expiry cron marks the signature and cancels the HelloSign request) / `FAILED` (delivery or signing error — see `error`). The `expiry` timestamp is computed at trigger time as now + the template signatory's `validity`.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 datetime when the document was created.

output.description: Reference to the generated output file in object storage.

key.description: Object store URI for the generated file.

template.description: Reference to the template used to generate this document.

errors.description: Generation errors, if the document failed to produce output.

Document.description: A generated (or registered) document record. `output.key` is the storage URI of the rendered file; `signatures` tracks per-signatory e-signature state; `errors` is populated when generation fails.

key.description: Document key — used to derive the storage subject.
Key of the record to modify.

content.description: Base64-encoded template file content. The file is compiled with angular expression parser and any tag errors are reported — nothing is persisted.

TriggerOutputOverride.description: Per-trigger overrides for the template's stored `output` configuration. Any field provided here takes precedence; omitted fields fall back to the template, then to service defaults.

template.description: Key of the published template to trigger.

payload.description: Data context (source) for all template expressions. **No schema required — completely flexible and user-defined.** Every key in the payload becomes an identifier available in template tags. Example: payload `{"client_name": "Acme", "invoice_number": "INV-001"}` makes `{client_name}` and `{invoice_number}` available in the template. Nested objects and arrays are fully traversable: `{client.address.city}`, `{items.0.price}`, `{#items}...{/items}`. Missing fields render as empty (not errors) — use conditionals like `{#field}...{/}` to handle optional data. Structure your payload to match the identifiers referenced in your template; the API does not validate field matching.

list.description: One or more template trigger entries. Each queues an independent generation job rendered against the shared `payload`; per-entry `output` overrides take precedence over the template's stored output configuration.

subject.description: Messaging subject of the queued document (`ms.document.document.{sanitised filepath}`). Present on success — poll `GET /documents/{key}` with the corresponding key to observe generation progress.

errors.description: Validation or processing errors. Present on failure.
example: Document template with key: invoice-template does not have a template source

metadata.description: Optional data-point metadata about the aggregate.

results_total.description: Number of results in this response.

next_sequence.description: Sequence number to use for the next page.

total_messages.description: Total number of messages in the stream for this subject.

metadata.description: Optional data-point metadata about the aggregate.

results_total.description: Number of results in this response.

next_sequence.description: Sequence number to use for the next page.

total_messages.description: Total number of messages in the stream for this subject.

subject.description: Messaging subject of the created or updated record. Formats: draft template `ms.document.draft.template.{key}`, published template `ms.document.template.{key}`, document `ms.document.document.{key}` — with keys sanitised into subject tokens (`/` → `.`, spaces → `_`, other special characters → `uXXXX` codes).

signature_url.description: Embedded HelloSign signing URL, with `client_id` and `skip_domain_verification=true` already appended. Returned as snake_case `signature_url` at the gateway.

example.error: Authorization header with a bearer token is required

x-engine-gotchas: All routes are under the `/file-generator` gateway prefix. Single resources use a path param (`/file-generator/templates/{key}`), not `?key=`.

Update is PATCH (a merge-style upsert over the event stream); use the `/unset` routes to remove fields. Template unset is POST `/file-generator/templates/{key}/unset`; document unset is PATCH `/file-generator/documents/{key}/unset` (a gateway asymmetry).

Responses: the gateway returns the service `body` field directly (the HTTP status carries status_code). Reads => `{ body: <payload>, metadata? }` (lists: `body.results` / `body.results_total`). Mutations => the payload directly (`{subject}` | `{message:"success"}`); trigger => a bare array; validate => `{is_valid,errors}`. Errors => `{ error }`.

GET/PATCH on a missing OR deleted resource returns 500 `{ error: "resource not found" }` (404 is only a wrong route). PATCH to a non-existent template key is create-or-overwrite (silently creates a draft).

Trigger is asynchronous: the 200 is `[{template, subject} | {template, errors}]`; poll GET `/file-generator/documents/{key}`. A template with no resolvable output.content_type (override or stored) cannot be triggered.
Read aggregates carry extra event-sourcing fields (modified, sequence, subject, type) that are not part of the writable schema.

The service also has AI-generation handlers (pptx, docx-generator, docx-editor, pdf-python, xlsx, html-pdf) but they are NOT in the gateway route registry (quiva-endpoints.json) and are not REST-callable.
